name: The number finally moves, and the archive says so
non_visual_rationale: The observables are three fields on a published call -- the effective wave height, the size band and the integer score -- plus two fields on the archived row. They reach a rendered page through the region bundle, and this step measures them at the bundle, which is the producer's own boundary. The rendering surface itself is unchanged by this step: no template, no string, no style is touched. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A here. The claim that the move survives all the way to a real published artefact is NOT left to the tests: it is proven separately through the shipped CLI and recorded under real_surface_proof in the 02-06 contract.
why_no_production_change: The capability was already delivered and is already wired. 02-02 shipped applyCorrection's clamped per-key height move and its signed, saturated score move. 02-03 shipped the read that hands a real record to it. build.ts has subtracted memberHBias from every member's raw height and passed correction.delta_q into combine since before this step, and it archives bias_applied and bias_gate on every row. What was missing was not code but PROOF at the surface a surfer reads: until this step, every record any acceptance test had driven through the builder was one the gates refused, so no test had ever watched a published number actually move. This step is that watch. Per the methodology's own rule -- if the acceptance test passes without new production code, that is CORRECT and no code may be added to manufacture a diff -- nothing under src/ was touched, and `git diff --stat src/` is deliberately empty.
criteria_delivered: 1. With a passing record on file the published height rises by the applied member bias and the score moves by the applied delta. Both halves are measured EXACTLY, and neither restates a production formula in the test. The height claim is metamorphic: a third build is run whose prediction log already forecasts the corrected metres and which has no correction file at all, and the corrected build must publish the same wave. It does, to 1.1e-15 (1.7554358433164114 against 1.7554358433164108) -- the same metres reached by two orders of operation, lift-then-average against average-then-lift -- so the assertion allows 1e-9 and says why. The published size_band must match that control build too, and it does: both read head_overhead where day zero read chest_head. The score claim rides the same control: two builds publishing the same wave differ only by the applied delta, and the corrected build scores exactly 9 points below the control (77 against 86), which is exactly the display points the record earned.

2. The archived call carries bias_gate applied and bias_applied equal to MINUS the record's score b over 100. Asserted as an exact float equality against the record's OWN stated b, computed in the test from the file rather than read off the row it is checking.

3. The prior build's archived rows are untouched; the new build appends its own. Two builds three hours apart against ONE durable universe: the earlier build's archived bytes are captured before the second build runs and asserted byte-identical after it, and the later build's own rows exist under its own build hour. Guarded against a vacuous pass by first asserting the later build genuinely moved the number.
scope_note: The accepted roadmap names src/learning/load-correction.ts and tests/unit/learning-apply-recheck.test.ts. Neither is touched. load-correction.ts needed no change because 02-03 already made it hand real records to the builder, and inventing an edit there to satisfy a file list would be manufacturing a diff. learning-apply-recheck.test.ts is a unit file over the pure applyCorrection port; every claim this step makes is about what runBuildOnce PUBLISHES, which that file cannot see. The proof lands in the one Vitest acceptance file the roadmap gives all four of steps 02-03 through 02-06, which is where its describe block sits.
acceptance: Two examples through runBuildOnce. (1) A record whose every key clears every rung on its own stated evidence publishes exactly what a forecast of the corrected metres publishes, moves the score down by exactly the earned display points, archives applied with the exact bias, and moves no number at the spot beside it. (2) A second build of the same morning, against the same store, with the file added between them, leaves the first build's archived bytes exactly as they were and archives its own rows under its own hour.
fixture_arithmetic: MEASURED against the real emitter before a single assertion was written, not derived from an earlier step's recorded numbers -- and that mattered: the figures carried in 02-02's contract for a similar fixture (score b 12.0, height b 0.60) do NOT hold for this one, and writing assertions around them would have produced tests that were wrong in a way only a fixture change could expose. At 18 paired mornings from 6 people, one reported band and one shown score of 79, buildCorrectionRecords writes a height key of b -0.18 m and a score key of b 9.0 display points, both on se 0.0566 m and 2.946 points -- the physical floor alone, since every observation agrees -- and both clear their own ladder by better than double. The negative height difference is the honest direction for this fixture: the models ran SMALL against what people saw, so a corrected member goes UP and the published band rises a step. 0.18 m is deliberately well inside the 0.48 m that forty percent of a 1.2 m member allows, because this step's claim is that the number moves by what was ordered; whether a bigger order is bounded is 02-05's claim, and a saturating fixture here would have proved that one instead of this one. Both facts are asserted in the test as anti-vacuity guards rather than assumed.
test_budget: Three behaviours: the published wave follows the applied member bias; the published score follows the applied delta and the archive states it; an earlier build's archive survives a later build. Budget 2 x 3 = 6. Delivered 2 acceptance examples. The first carries two behaviours because they share one fixture and one control build, and splitting them would have run the same three builds twice to assert halves of one claim.
unit_law: NONE ADDED. Every arithmetic claim under this step is already quantified over its whole generated space by 02-02's fast-check laws in tests/unit/learning-apply-recheck.test.ts -- the score move's sign and saturation, and the per-key height move's exactness and saturation. What was missing was never coverage of the arithmetic; it was proof that the arithmetic reaches a published number. That is an acceptance-level claim by construction and a unit law cannot make it.
red_evidence: This step adds no production code, so RED was established the only honest way available: against the SHIPPED body, by controlled mutation, watching each new assertion reject a build that stops doing the thing. Three mutations of src/pipeline/build.ts, each planted alone and reverted, typecheck clean under each so every red was behavioural, zero collection errors. (1) The applied score delta never reaches combine (`correction.delta_q` -> `0`): 1 failure, 'the published score must fall by the 9 display points the record earned, and by nothing else: the same wave scored 86 with no file and 86 with one'. (2) The applied member bias never reaches the published wave (the `- correction.memberHBias(...)` subtraction dropped): 1 failure, 'a correction of 0.1800000000000002 m must publish the wave a forecast 0.1800000000000002 m different publishes: it published 1.531337650552614 m against 1.7554358433164114 m'. (3) Every build of a day archives under one key (`build=${hour}Z` pinned to `build=12Z`): 1 failure in the append example, the later build having no archive of its own. Each mutation failed exactly one example and left the other four green, which is the evidence that these are three separate claims and not one assertion in three costumes.
falsifiability_evidence: The three mutations above ARE the falsifiability proof; there is no separate production change to break. After each revert `git diff --stat src/` was empty and `git status --short` named only this step's test file. The litmus the methodology asks for -- revert the production code and see whether the tests still pass -- is answered directly by mutations 1 and 2: with either lane cut, the tests go red. These tests cannot pass on fixture state.
gates_run: npm run typecheck exit 0. Full vitest 452/452 across 85 files, up from 450/85, which is exactly this step's two examples. One flake was hit and chased rather than accepted: tests/unit/report-island.test.ts failed twice on 'ENOTEMPTY: rename node_modules/.vite/deps_temp_... -> deps' inside the temporary project copy it builds. That is a vite dependency-optimiser race in a temp directory, it names no assertion of this feature, and the file passes 14/14 on its own and in a clean full run. Recorded rather than hidden.
float_equality_note: One assertion in this step is a tolerance rather than an equality, and the reason is stated in the test beside it: the corrected build and the control build compute the same metres by different orders of operation, so they agree to about 1e-15 rather than bit for bit. The tolerance is 1e-9, six orders of magnitude tighter than the smallest move any of these fixtures makes (0.18 m), so it cannot swallow a real regression. Every other assertion in this step is exact.
